title: Rajendra Kumar Agarwal v. State of U.P.
coram: Huluvadi G. Ramesh, J.; Shamsher Bahadur Singh, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; petitioner relegated to appeal on depositing Rs. 2 lakh.
headnote: A demand imposing a theft penalty of Rs. 3,31,957/-, challenged as lacking a final assessment and statutory compliance, was not interfered with in writ jurisdiction because disputed questions of fact were involved. The High Court disposed of the petition, granting fifteen days to file an appeal, directing the appellate authority to decide it in accordance with law within three months, and requiring a deposit of Rs. 2,00,000/-, with the balance subject to the appeal.
facts: The Executive Engineer, Electricity Distribution Division-II, Firozabad, issued a demand dated 21 November 2015 assessing alleged electricity theft and imposing a penalty of Rs. 3,31,957/- on Rajendra Kumar Agarwal. He contended that no final assessment had been passed and that the demand lacked basis and statutory compliance. He sought quashing of the demand, an enquiry by the Committee under Clause 8.0 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and restraint against disconnection and recovery.

holding_units.topic: theft penalty — writ jurisdiction and statutory appeal
holding_units.holding: A writ challenging a theft-assessment demand and penalty will not be entertained where disputed questions of fact are involved. The consumer was given fifteen days to file an appeal; the appellate authority was directed to dispose of it in accordance with law within three months; deposit of Rs. 2,00,000/- was required, with the remaining amount subject to the result of the appeal.

not_decided.point: Validity of the theft assessment, demand notice dated 21.11.2015, and penalty of Rs. 3,31,957/-, including compliance with the Electricity Act and Clause 8.0 of the Supply Code
not_decided.note: Declined on disputed questions of fact; relegated to the appellate authority
